title: RAND vs RANDBETWEEN vs RANDARRAY: three flavors of random
meta_desc: RAND vs RANDBETWEEN vs RANDARRAY: decimals, integers, and whole grids; volatility, freezing values, and version support verified by execution.
intro: One value or a grid, decimals or integers: the random family splits by shape and type. All three share the same gotcha — volatility — and the same cure (Paste Special → Values).

cols: A whole spilled grid — decimals or integers
Yes — the whole grid at once

when.use_when: Probabilities and continuous values — coin flips (RAND()<0.5), jittering chart points, random sort keys.
Dice, test scores, sample IDs — anything that must be a whole number in a range.
Bulk generation on modern versions — one formula fills a table, and SORTBY(range,RANDARRAY(n)) is the clean shuffle idiom.

compat_note: RAND and RANDBETWEEN execute in every LibreOffice version we test (Excel behavior per docs — we do not run desktop Excel; Google Sheets is executed separately, see each function page); RANDARRAY is verified supported in LibreOffice 25.8 (our harness asserts its deterministic properties — shape and bounds — since the values themselves change per recalc). All three are volatile everywhere: freeze results with Paste Special → Values, or they re-roll on every edit. Excel for the web is a separate application and we do execute it (recalculated on OneDrive, 2026-09-01); those measurements are on the individual function pages.
